title: The $100 Lens Sanduk Ruit Set Out to Make for $4 in Kathmandu
conflicts: Imported lens price given as US$100 (Ruit, Himalayan Times), US$150 (Nepali Times 2012) or US$200 (HCP nomination); Tilganga's price US$4 (Ruit), under US$5 (Magsaysay) or US$3 (Kathmandu Post 2018). Story uses Ruit's own figures and the citation's 'under $5'. Founding year 1994 in most sources, 1992 in an IAPB nomination; story uses 1994. Lens totals rise by date (1.5m in 2006, 3m in 2012, 5m in 2018); only the 2006 figure is used.
notes: Ruit's 2006 Down To Earth interview is the main founder source (motive to escape bureaucracy, failed first lens attempt, 1994-96 development, donated land, self-sustaining by 2006). Avery's 2018 press release is self-interested and its claims are attributed. Hollows's death year is not stated because the cited sources say only that he died before Tilganga and the laboratory opened. Company field uses 'Tilganga Eye Centre' only; the repeat screen flags Aravind Eye Hospital on the word 'Eye' but lets it through. Reflection touches imported kits and equipment without naming talQen.
